html:
The Salvadoran Civil War was fought from 1979 to 1992 between the military government of El Salvador and the guerrillas of the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front. About 75,000 people were killed, most of them civilians killed by the army and death squads.

Its roots lay in land hunger, the coffee oligarchy and fifty years of army rule since La Matanza. The killing of Archbishop Romero in 1980 and of thousands of others pushed many into the guerrilla. The United States, fearing another Nicaragua during the Cold War, gave the army billions of dollars in aid.

Neither side could win. After a guerrilla offensive reached the capital in 1989 and soldiers murdered six Jesuit priests, both sides accepted UN talks, which led to the Chapultepec Peace Accords. Hundreds of thousands fled, many to the United States, the start of the Salvadoran diaspora.
